history.period: Ancient (claimed 9th century CE / Puranic); rebuilt 18th century
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: documented at Bhairavgarh (Bhairugarh), ~4.5-8 km north of Ujjain city, not in Ujjain town itself (source distances CONFLICT (verify): 4-5 km per tourmyindia/earthtrip, 8 km per bhasmarti). Temple of Kal Bhairav - the fierce manifestation of Shiva, revered as the guardian (Kotwal) of Ujjain - on the banks of the Kshipra. It finds mention in the Avanti Khanda of the Skanda Purana; local tradition claims great antiquity ('6,000 years' - legendary, unverified) and one source attributes a 9th-century build to King Bhadrasena (unverified). The stone temple was rebuilt in the 18th century by Maratha general Maharaja Mahadji Scindia of Gwalior, whose turban-offering legend is still commemorated (the idol wears a Maratha-style pagri). World-famous for the unique ritual of offering liquor (madira) to the deity, poured into a saucer held to the idol's lips; devotees also offer mustard oil, coconuts and flowers. Maratha-style architecture with wall paintings; stray dogs near the temple are fed in reverence (the dog is Bhairav's vahana).

name: Kal Bhairav Temple
town: Bhairavgarh, ~4.5-8 km north of Ujjain (CSV town 'Ujjain' is the nearby city)
town_description: Ujjain, on the banks of the Kshipra River, is one of the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela every 12 years. It is an ancient centre of astronomy and Shaivism, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and a rich cluster of temples including Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, and Mangalnath.
